title: Aspiring writer-director here. I’ve got a question.

commenti.body:
For me, the concept is nothing, the execution is everything. Something profound can be made out of a banal concept, and something truly unwatchable can be made out of a clever premise.

If you have to get a spec script optioned by a studio, it's a little more important to grab them with the elevator pitch, but if you want to direct your own material, that's a little less vital. Work on short film concepts you can fund yourself, shorts that can play well for a festival audience, and try to make a name for yourself that way so you can eventually get to a place where someone (maybe even a studio) will fund your next, more expensive, idea.

That said, if this was /r/screenwriting and you wanted advice on how those pitches will go over in an industry context, I'd say your first two are a lot more sellable than your third. Also if I'm reading your second premise correctly, and it's from the perspective of someone suspecting a classmate of those crimes, it's really more like Rear Window than Psycho.

I’d rate these as the same question you keep asking here again and again week after week instead of just trusting your instincts and making something or starting to make it. Just make something. Pick one you like and do it. Make a short. Shoot a scene. Write a script. Write all three. Make a look book or a rip-o-matic.

Do something and stop imagining that concept alone really matters much at all.

It’s literally all about the execution.

How you do something and how well you do it is almost infinitely more important to whether it succeeds artistically and connects with audiences than what the concept is.

A good concept is about only always and ever about marketing. Whereas great execution is about making something worthwhile that others see the worth in.

So if you don’t believe enough in one of these three ideas to start making it, why should any audience or any producer?

And why do you only have 3 ideas you keep repeating? Get some more ideas. Generate at least one a day or a few a week. Sit with them a while. Flesh them out more.
